statement: The supplied sources do not contain a derivation of the method of Lagrange multipliers. The method of Lagrange multipliers is defined as a strategy for finding local maxima and minima of an objective function f subject to equation constraints g = 0 by finding stationary points of the Lagrangian function, defined by the condition \nabla_{x, \lambda} \mathcal{L}(x, \lambda) = \nabla_{x, \lambda} (f(x) + \lambda \cdot g(x)) = 0.

symbols.meaning: Lagrangian function combining the objective function and constraint equations
objective function to be maximized or minimized
constraint function defining the equation constraint g = 0
Lagrange multiplier associated with the constraint
gradient operator with respect to variables and multipliers

properties.property: Stationary points of the Lagrangian satisfy the original constraint equations.
properties.why: Differentiating the Lagrangian with respect to the multiplier lambda yields the constraint equation g = 0.

properties.property: Critical points of the Lagrangian occur at saddle points rather than local maxima or minima of the Lagrangian.
properties.why: The Hessian matrix of the Lagrangian evaluated at the critical points is indefinite.

properties.property: The stationarity condition identifies constrained extrema even where objective level sets are not tangent to constraints.
properties.why: Extrema can occur where lambda = 0 and level curves of f are not tangent to the constraint.

properties.property: Standard numerical extremum-seeking algorithms cannot be applied directly to the Lagrangian function.
properties.why: Techniques like gradient descent or hill climbing search for local extrema rather than saddle points.

assumptions.assumption: Constraints are equality equation constraints that must be satisfied exactly.
assumptions.breaks_when: Constraints are inequalities or cannot be expressed as exact equations.

assumptions.assumption: The objective function and constraint functions are differentiable with respect to their variables.
assumptions.breaks_when: The objective f or constraint g is non-differentiable or has undefined partial derivatives.

assumptions.assumption: The numerical solver used directly on the Lagrangian locates general stationary points rather than extrema.
assumptions.breaks_when: An algorithm designed strictly for local minimization or maximization (such as gradient descent) is run directly on the Lagrangian.

failure_modes.mode: Numerical optimization divergence on the Lagrangian
failure_modes.signature: Optimization fails to converge or diverges when using local extremum seekers directly on the Lagrangian.
failure_modes.cause: Critical points of the Lagrangian are saddle points with indefinite Hessian matrices rather than local extrema.

failure_modes.mode: Division by zero during algebraic solving of stationary conditions
failure_modes.signature: Singular expressions or omitted solutions when solving equations where coordinates are expressed with lambda in the denominator.
failure_modes.cause: Assuming lambda != 0 when isolating variables, which fails to capture candidate extrema where lambda = 0.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so lagrange_multipliers is recorded as a definition
